[page[title]]

C# source files must use one consistent line-ending style throughout the project.

What The Standard says

“Readability” — The Standard values a codebase that is immediately readable and standardized. Mixed line endings create invisible variation and noisy tooling changes without conveying intent. read it here.
“consistent handling” — The Standard explicitly favors consistency across implementations. The analyser leaves the platform-specific line-ending choice open but requires the project to make one consistent choice. read it here.

Why it matters

The Standard does not require CRLF or LF; it does value consistency and low-friction collaboration. Mixed endings create whole-file diffs and recurring editor warnings, so the analyser enforces one project-wide style while leaving the actual style to the project.

Bad code example

// Violates STXFORMAT013: C# source files must use one consistent line-ending style throughout the project.
// Student.cs uses LF, while the project uses CRLF
class Student { }

Good code example

// Follows STXFORMAT013
// Every C# file in this project uses the same line endings
class Student { }
